title: Ines and the Safehouse
premise: Wendell Blackwood, a private security contractor who has spent a decade keeping his head down, receives a meeting invitation from his handler—sent after the man's funeral. The invitation leads him to Ines Marchetti, a cryptographer defecting from the very firm that employs Wendell, and he is ordered to extract her to a safehouse that may not exist on any official map. As Wendell realizes the dead handler left him a trail of evidence exposing the firm's corruption of its own government clients, he must choose between the duty that has defined him and the woman who may be bait in someone else's trap. Betrayed by his own team and hunted through a city that keeps rewriting its rules, Wendell sacrifices his anonymity to expose the firm, ending with him and Ines walking away with the truth made public—and his old life permanently burned.
about_author: Isandro Almeida is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent years working alongside private security firms before turning to fiction. He writes lean, paranoid thrillers about ordinary professionals trapped inside systems designed to consume them.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV: Wendell. At his handler Marcus Hale's sparsely attended funeral, Wendell receives an automated calendar invite from Marcus's account—for tomorrow, 6 a.m., a diner outside the city. He checks the metadata: sent two hours ago. The beat is quiet dread; the rules that kept him safe for ten years have just been broken by a dead man.

chapters.title: Diner at Six
chapters.summary: POV: Wendell. No Marcus—but a woman waits, Ines Marchetti, claiming Marcus hired her to decrypt a ledger before he died. She slides Wendell a drive and vanishes when two men in firm windbreakers enter. Wendell decrypts fragments overnight: payments routing to officials. Emotional beat: the first crack in his loyalty.

chapters.title: Chain of Custody
chapters.summary: POV: Wendell. His new handler, Director Voss, orders him to extract 'an asset' to Safehouse Kestrel—a site Wendell has never heard of in ten years. The asset's file photo is Ines. Wendell realizes he's being used as deniable muscle, and that Marcus's death was ruled accidental too cleanly. Beat: controlled fear sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Ines
chapters.summary: POV: Ines. She watches Wendell approach her safe flat and lets him in, testing whether he's hunter or escort. Their wary negotiation reveals she decrypted Marcus's full ledger: the firm sells client data to hostile buyers. She trusts Marcus's judgment of Wendell more than Wendell does. Beat: reluctant alliance, first flicker of mutual respect.

chapters.title: Kestrel
chapters.summary: POV: Wendell. The extraction goes wrong—the safehouse is a kill box, staffed by contractors Wendell trained himself. He and Ines escape through service tunnels as the building burns behind them. Someone inside the firm wanted both of them erased. Beat: betrayal made physical; no going back.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Off-grid in a rented basement, they piece together Marcus's dead-drop chain while Voss floods the city with their descriptions. Ines reveals Marcus was her uncle's partner decades ago; the ledger was personal before it was leverage. Wendell teaches her tradecraft; she teaches him what he's been protecting all along. Beat: intimacy under pressure.

chapters.title: The Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: POV: Wendell. Wendell confronts his oldest colleague, Reyes, who admits the firm has owned its government oversight committee for six years—and offers Wendell reinstatement if he delivers Ines. Wendell records the conversation. Beat: temptation offered plainly, and refused; duty inverts into purpose.

chapters.title: Dead Drop
chapters.summary: POV: Ines. Following Marcus's final instructions, they retrieve the original ledger from a storage unit—along with a letter naming Voss personally and predicting his own death. Voss's team ambushes them; Reyes unexpectedly covers their escape and is wounded. Beat: grief and fury fused; the plan crystallizes.

chapters.title: Six A.M., Tomorrow
chapters.summary: POV: Wendell. Climax. Wendell walks into Voss's office wearing a wire, offering Ines in exchange for his old life, buying minutes while Ines broadcasts the ledger to every client, journalist, and regulator on Marcus's list. Voss realizes too late that the meeting invitation was always the trap—inverted. Beat: cold clarity, maximum tension.

chapters.title: Afterimage
chapters.summary: POV: Ines. Weeks later: arrests, hearings, the firm dissolved. Wendell, officially nonexistent, meets Ines where Marcus's letter asked them to scatter his ashes. They carry nothing but each other and the memory of who they were before. Final beat: love chosen over duty, memory honored over erasure—an open road instead of a safehouse.
